note: The Library: official PDFs, each opened and checked. `year` is read from the PDF itself (`year_from` says where: a printed date, or the file's own date when none is printed). `checked` is the day the original_url last answered with a real PDF; `sha256` is of that file. `mirror` is our unchanged copy in library/, kept only when `rights` is public-domain or license-allows; otherwise null and the card links to the publisher. `sections` are the site's section keys, first one is the shelf it sits on. `states` is empty for national documents. `stale`: more than 8 years old with no newer edition, kept because nothing newer covers the topic as well (its `why` says so). Re-check with node scripts/check-library.mjs; rebuild the zip with node scripts/build-library-zip.mjs. Dropped documents and the reasons are in DECISIONS.md, D-102 to D-108.
intro: The guides the experts publish, in one place: FEMA, the CDC, the Weather Service, the Red Cross, the pediatricians, the states. This is a reference shelf, not more to read. Print the short shelf below before you need it, and come back for the rest when a section of the plan sends you here.
print_first_intro: Eight documents a household should have on paper before the power goes out: the kit checklist, the family contact plan, how to make water safe, what to throw out of the fridge, the papers to copy, the steps to stop bleeding, and your state’s guide. Print them, put them in a folder by the grab bag, and you have the core of the plan with no phone and no power.
sky_line: One useful thing to do in the first hour: print the eight documents on the library’s short shelf while the printer still works.

shelf_intro.first: Plans to fill in by hand, and the state and city guides that go with them.
shelf_intro.household: Fire in an apartment building, and bleeding.
shelf_intro.bag: Kit lists, the papers to copy, and what to pack for babies and pets.
shelf_intro.h72: Water, food, power, cold, heat, storms, and the first hours after a nuclear explosion.
shelf_intro.w2: The long guides, and two weeks of water and food.
shelf_intro.keep: Keeping going once the big lists are done.

how: Every document here was found on its publisher’s own website, downloaded, opened and read on the date shown. Where the publisher is the US federal government, the site keeps an exact copy, so the link still works when an agency moves its page. Everything else opens at the publisher. Nothing here has been edited, compressed or re-branded. The library is re-checked every three months.
